candidate.name: Pasito
candidate.description: AI agents for insurance and benefits
candidate.long_description:
Pasito builds AI agents for insurance and benefits—transforming how benefits are built, delivered, and experienced.

Our Core AI ingests and understands plan documents and employee census data to build structured benefit intelligence.

Our Engagement AI Agents orchestrate complex workflows—powering decision support, plan comparisons, guides, highlight sheets, microsites, communications, claims reminders, RFP management, document audits, translations, and more—all from a single intelligent database.

With Pasito, carriers, brokers, and benefits vendors eliminate manual work, accelerate growth, and deliver the personalized benefits experiences employees deserve—all powered by compliant, scalable AI systems.

Backed by Y Combinator, Core Innovation Capital, and other leading investors.

score.thesis: AI-native autonomous agents owning high-value business workflows

analysis.team: Pasito was founded by Pauline Roteta (co-founder and CEO). Before Pasito she was a Senior Investor & Portfolio Manager at BlackRock, and she holds credentials as a Certified Financial Planner, CFA, Fulbright Scholar, and a B.Eng. from Vanderbilt University (Founder bio: Pauline Roteta). Her financial/investing background is relevant to the insurance and benefits domain, though the sources do not describe her technical/engineering track record in building AI systems, and the bio references a co-founder without naming a second person. The team is 20 people (YC profile).
analysis.product: Pasito builds AI agents for insurance and benefits (YC one-liner). Its Core AI ingests plan documents and employee census data to build structured 'benefit intelligence,' while its Engagement AI Agents orchestrate complex workflows including decision support, plan comparisons, guides, highlight sheets, microsites, communications, claims reminders, RFP management, document audits, and translations — all from a single database (YC long description). Customers are carriers, brokers, and benefits vendors, who use it to eliminate manual work and deliver personalized benefits experiences (YC long description).
analysis.market: The company targets carriers, brokers, and benefits vendors in the insurance and benefits space, tagged across Fintech, Insurance, Health Tech, and AI (YC profile). The sources give no market-size figures, no named competitors, and no explicit why-now thesis, so market attractiveness, TAM, and competitive positioning are unknown from the provided material and should be treated as open questions.
risks: Autonomy is unproven: while the product uses 'AI agents' and workflow language, the sources do not explicitly describe autonomous, self-directed operation, so it may be assistive rather than truly agentic (YC long description; score breakdown notes 0/15 on autonomy).

Single named founder: only Pauline Roteta is named despite 'co-founder' language, and there is no stated technical/AI engineering lead, raising questions about founding-team completeness (Founder bio: Pauline Roteta).

Regulatory and compliance exposure: operating across insurance, benefits, and health data involves compliance risk; the description claims 'compliant, scalable AI systems' but provides no evidence or detail (YC long description).
No traction or revenue signals: the sources provide no customer counts, revenue, or growth metrics, so commercial validation is unknown (source material).
what_would_change_our_mind: Evidence that the AI agents act autonomously end-to-end on high-value workflows (e.g., closing RFPs or resolving claims tasks without human steps) rather than assisting a human operator.
Named, referenceable carrier/broker/vendor customers plus revenue or retention metrics demonstrating commercial traction.
Clarity on the founding team's technical depth and a complete founder/leadership roster building the AI systems.
analysis.recommendation_rationale: Pasito scores 58 (Watch): it is clearly AI-native and owns a real, high-value workflow across benefits and insurance, but the sources show no explicit autonomy language and thin freshness, momentum, and team signals. The financially credentialed founder and 20-person team are encouraging, yet the lack of stated technical depth, unnamed co-founder, and absence of traction or market data leave the thesis fit unconfirmed. This warrants monitoring rather than conviction until autonomy and commercial validation are demonstrated.
